answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making trust expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Each identity earns a public record of attested work, so a newcomer starts at the nadir of reputation and must climb slowly. Cheap copies stall in a shallow lagoon of unverified claims, while honest agents become a beacon: peers check their history before transacting, and forging a thousand credible histories costs a thousand times the effort, so mass fakery stops paying.
